V1.OBJECT: A physical, biological, technical or digital object, system, component or artifact; a concrete entity rather than an abstract concept or method.
V1.ACTOR: A person, organization, institution, state or other participant acting as a subject in context; a physical object causing change is not automatically an actor.
V1.CONCEPT: An abstract concept, theory, mathematical construction, scientific category or hypothesis, rather than a concrete object or method.
V1.METHOD: A defined way to perform, study, analyze or compute something: an algorithm, procedure, technology or experimental technique; the way to solve a task rather than the task or its execution.
V1.PROCESS: An action, operation, event, change or sequence of occurring actions; the occurrence itself, rather than a method, object or necessarily an explanatory mechanism.
V1.DATA_RESOURCE: A dataset, corpus, registry, archive, sample or source of organized information, distinct from the object described by the information.
V1.ATTRIBUTE: A property, parameter, measurable characteristic or metric; the characteristic itself rather than a particular obtained result or an explicit condition.
V1.RESULT: An observed, measured, computed or established outcome of a study, experiment, method or process; a particular obtained outcome rather than the metric itself.
V1.CONDITION: An explicit experimental, observational or applicability condition under which a statement holds; not simply an abstract concept or a characteristic.
V1.TASK: A task, goal, problem or application area to be addressed, rather than the method used to solve it.
V1.MECHANISM: A mechanism described in the source that explains how or why a phenomenon occurs; not every process and not merely an object involved.

V2.OBJECT: A physical, biological, technical or digital object, system, component or artifact; a concrete entity rather than an abstract concept or method. Examples: a robot; a concrete neural network model.
V2.ACTOR: A person, organization, institution, state or other participant acting as a subject in context; a physical object causing change is not automatically an actor. Examples: a university; a government.
V2.CONCEPT: An abstract concept, theory, mathematical construction, scientific category or hypothesis, rather than a concrete object or method. Examples: game theory; a topological space.
V2.METHOD: A defined way to perform, study, analyze or compute something: an algorithm, procedure, technology or experimental technique; the way to solve a task rather than the task or its execution. Examples: spectroscopy; the Monte Carlo method.
V2.PROCESS: An action, operation, event, change or sequence of occurring actions; the occurrence itself, rather than a method, object or necessarily an explanatory mechanism. Examples: cell division; chemical reaction.
V2.DATA_RESOURCE: A dataset, corpus, registry, archive, sample or source of organized information, distinct from the object described by the information. Examples: a text corpus; a medical registry.
V2.ATTRIBUTE: A property, parameter, measurable characteristic or metric; the characteristic itself rather than a particular obtained result or an explicit condition. Examples: mass; classification accuracy as a metric.
V2.RESULT: An observed, measured, computed or established outcome of a study, experiment, method or process; a particular obtained outcome rather than the metric itself. Examples: 94% accuracy; a measured reduction in mortality.
V2.CONDITION: An explicit experimental, observational or applicability condition under which a statement holds; not simply an abstract concept or a characteristic. Examples: room temperature; fasting state.
V2.TASK: A task, goal, problem or application area to be addressed, rather than the method used to solve it. Examples: image classification; route optimization.
V2.MECHANISM: A mechanism described in the source that explains how or why a phenomenon occurs; not every process and not merely an object involved. Examples: immune response mechanism; disease causal mechanism.
